newsitem.title: FRANCE: CGIP offers "French solution" for Valeo.
newsitem.headline: CGIP offers "French solution" for Valeo.

text.p: Industrial holding group CGIP offered a "French solution" to the future of car parts maker Valeo on Thursday, proposing to sell some of its assets to buy a 28 percent stake from Italian financier Carlo De Benedetti.

CGIP said it wanted to conclude negotiations to buy the stake held by De Benedetti's French holding company Cerus and would offer for sale of half of its stake in U.S. packaging giant Crown Cork and Seal to help to finance the deal.
It said it would remain Crown Cork's largest shareholder with 10 percent of the stock.
The French government and French car manufacturers have been trying to arrange a French purchase of the stake to fend off a buyout bid by U.S. or other foreign competitors.
Valeo, the second biggest car components group in Europe, is the leading supplier to PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault SA, France's two carmakers.
The statement confirmed reports that CGIP has been negotiating with Cerus to acquire its Valeo stake.

CGIP did not dislose the terms either of its offer to Cerus or of its proposed sale of Crown Cork shares, but Cerus's holding in Valeo is worth more than five billion francs ($970 million) at current market prices.
"(The board) expressed the wish that the discussions relating to the acquisiton of Cerus's holding in Valeo be completed," the CGIP statement said.

"Within this framework, the board authorised the offer for sale of almost half of CGIP's holding in Crowm Cork and Seal, the world's largest packaging company. With 10 percent of the stock, CGIP would remain its largest shareholder without any modification of the existing agreements."
It added that Crown Cork had said it was proceeding with preliminary formalities required by U.S. stock exchange authorities for an offering expected in late October.
CGIP earlier this month denied it was planning to launch takeover bids for either Cerus or Valeo.
Under French bourse rules, the purchase of less than 33 pct of a company's share capital does not require a public takeover offer.
